correctness.rationale: The one-component family has ordinary frame operator \(S_\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(4,1)\) and exact ordinary bounds \(1,4\). The chosen controller \(U\) has exact eigenvalues \(1/10,19/10\), while \(T=K=I\) makes every explicit commutation hypothesis of the source theorem hold. At \(f=(1,-2)\), the controlled quadratic form equals \(-1\), so no positive lower controlled bound exists. Under pairwise commutation, the operator inequality \(c_-S_\Lambda\le TU S_\Lambda\le c_+S_\Lambda\) proves both directions of the repaired theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem is an advertised equivalence connecting controlled and ordinary K-g-fusion frames. It fails in the smallest nontrivial dimension with a single g-fusion component and positive controllers, so the issue is structural rather than asymptotic or computational. The repair supplies a usable hypothesis and explicit two-way conversion of frame bounds.
